reference.headerSub: All {n} rules. No diagnosis run is required to view this page.
reference.error: Failed to load the rule list:

SEC-01.title: Eliminate legacy cipher suites
SEC-01.desc: Checks that SSIDs do not use WEP, TKIP, or open (unencrypted) authentication.

SEC-02.title: Apply OWE to open SSIDs
SEC-02.desc: Checks whether open (unencrypted) SSIDs use OWE (Enhanced Open) to encrypt traffic.

SEC-03.title: WPA3 migration status
SEC-03.desc: Checks whether SSIDs are still on WPA2 or have already migrated to WPA3 (or OWE).

SEC-04.title: PMF setting on WPA2 SSIDs
SEC-04.desc: Checks whether PMF (Protected Management Frames) is enabled on WPA2-family SSIDs via mfp-required or mfp-capable.

SEC-05.title: Avoid leaving WPA3 Transition Mode always on
SEC-05.desc: Checks whether WPA3 Transition Mode (co-existence with WPA2) is left permanently enabled. While enabled, WPA2-equivalent connections are still allowed.

SEC-06.title: WPA3 required on the 6GHz band
SEC-06.desc: Checks whether SSIDs using the 6GHz band satisfy the standard-mandated WPA3 (or OWE) requirement.

SEC-07.title: Wireless IDS detection (infrastructure) enabled
SEC-07.desc: Checks whether the WIDS detection level for infrastructure is off.

SEC-08.title: Wireless IDS detection (client) enabled
SEC-08.desc: Checks whether the WIDS detection level for clients is off.

SEC-09.title: Over-aggressive IDS detection level
SEC-09.desc: Checks whether the detection level is set high (medium/high), which can increase false positives.

SEC-10.title: Wireless containment enablement status
SEC-10.desc: Checks whether wireless containment is enabled. Because enabling it has implications for radio regulations and neighboring networks, a legal/security review is recommended.

SEC-11.title: High-risk protection policy enablement status
SEC-11.desc: Checks whether high-risk WIDS/WIPS protection policies such as rogue-containment are enabled. A legal/security review is recommended before enabling these.

SEC-12.title: Overall auth / key-distribution assessment (AI)
SEC-12.desc: The AI comments on auth server redundancy, whether each SSID's purpose matches its auth method, and where MPSK fits — based only on this run's snapshot.

SEC-13.title: SSID security posture (AI)
SEC-13.desc: The AI comments on which mechanical findings to fix first and on structural concerns the mechanical rules don't cover — based only on this run's snapshot.

RF-01.title: 2.4GHz channel width
RF-01.desc: Checks whether the 2.4GHz radio's channel width exceeds 20MHz.

RF-02.title: 5GHz channel width
RF-02.desc: Checks whether the 5GHz radio's channel width exceeds 80MHz.

RF-03.title: Consistent channel width within a band
RF-03.desc: Checks whether channel width is consistent across radios on the same band within a site.

RF-04.title: Restrict 2.4GHz to non-overlapping channels
RF-04.desc: Checks whether the allowed 2.4GHz channels are limited to the non-overlapping set (1/6/11).

RF-05.title: Tx power range within a radio
RF-05.desc: Checks whether the gap between a radio's max and min Tx power is too wide (which can keep ARM/RRM from converging).

RF-06.title: Tx power delta between 2.4GHz and 5GHz
RF-06.desc: Checks whether 5GHz minimum Tx power is set sufficiently higher than 2.4GHz (target: at least 6dB).

RF-07.title: Tx power delta between 5GHz and 6GHz
RF-07.desc: Checks whether 6GHz minimum Tx power falls within an appropriate range relative to 5GHz (target: 0 to +3dB).

RF-08.title: Basic rate floor
RF-08.desc: Checks whether low-speed rates (below 12Mbps) are included in the basic rates.

RF-10.title: OKC / PMK caching enabled
RF-10.desc: Checks whether OKC (Opportunistic Key Caching) is enabled.

RF-11.title: Broadcast/multicast filtering enabled
RF-11.desc: Checks whether the broadcast filter and IPv6 RA filter are enabled.

RF-12.title: Wi-Fi 6/7 feature disablement status
RF-12.desc: Checks whether HE (Wi-Fi 6) / EHT (Wi-Fi 7) features have been unintentionally disabled.

RF-13.title: ARM (Adaptive Radio Management) enabled
RF-13.desc: Checks whether ARM scanning / client-match is enabled (AOS8 only).

RF-14.title: Mixed AP model series
RF-14.desc: Checks whether AP model series (e.g. the 5xx and 6xx families) are mixed within a site.

RF-15.title: 2.4GHz handling in high-density environments (AI)
RF-15.desc: Given the SSIDs using 2.4GHz and the AP count, the AI comments on whether 2.4GHz should stay open for client use here, explicitly noting this is environment-dependent.

RF-16.title: Validity of static channel/power assignment vs. RRM (AI)
RF-16.desc: The AI comments on whether channels/power are being left to AirMatch / ARM / Mist RRM, or whether static assignments remain in place.

SEC-01.wep: {ssid}: uses WEP ({opmode}). Migrate this as a priority.
SEC-01.pairwiseUnset: {ssid}: the pairwise cipher is not explicitly set — left to Mist's default.

SEC-02.openNotOwe: {ssid}: open authentication without OWE — traffic is not encrypted.

SEC-03.wpa2: {ssid}: still on WPA2. Consider migrating to WPA3.
SEC-03.legacy: {ssid}: legacy cipher — not applicable here (see SEC-01).
SEC-03.pairwiseUnset: {ssid}: the cipher is not explicitly set — cannot determine.

SEC-04.required: {ssid}: mfp-required is set — PMF is mandatory.
SEC-04.capableOnly: {ssid}: only mfp-capable is set — PMF is optional. Consider enabling mfp-required.
SEC-04.capableViaMbo: {ssid}: mbo-enable implicitly enables PMF (capable). Consider explicitly enabling mfp-required.
SEC-04.disabled: {ssid}: neither mfp-capable nor mfp-required is set — PMF is disabled.
SEC-04.notWpa2: {ssid}: not a WPA2-family SSID — not applicable (PMF is decided automatically by opmode).

coach.title: Coach
coach.sub: A study buddy that turns our own records into hints — not answers
coach.pool: Teaching material: {knowledge} approved knowledge entries / {history} investigation records / {rules} best practices

chat.title: Talk it through
chat.greeting: What's giving you trouble? Rough words are fine — just type it as it comes.
chat.placeholder: Tell me what you're stuck on (⌘/Ctrl + Enter to send)
chat.failed: Sorry, that didn't go through. Try sending it again.
chat.hintMoreTitle: Get one step more of a hint
chat.escalateTitle: Skip the hints and hear the answer with the reasoning
chat.investigateTitle: For a deep dive, go to the Network Investigation tab. Coach checks the current state when it needs to, but digging deep is that tab’s job.
chat.incidentTitle: Turn this on and Coach answers straight away, no hints first
chat.incidentNote: Incident mode. No struggling — I'll lead with the answer. Turn it off once things settle and we can go back to thinking out loud.
chat.generalOnly: Our own records have nothing on this, so I'm going off general advice here.

pool.p01: There's a rogue AP alert — where do I even start?
pool.p02: Someone says a switch went down. What do I check first?
pool.p03: What's actually bad about mixing WPA2 and WPA3?
pool.p04: A client won't roam to the closer AP and just sticks to the far one — what's going on?
pool.p05: I'm trying to steer clients to 5GHz but they keep sitting on 2.4GHz. Why?
pool.p06: One corner of the floor has weak signal — does that mean the RF design needs a redo?
pool.p07: I'm seeing an unknown AP broadcasting the same SSID — is that dangerous?
pool.p08: What actually changes if I drop the channel width from 80MHz to 40MHz?
pool.p09: Should I prioritize 6GHz or 5GHz in the design?
pool.p10: An AP that should be getting PoE won't power on — what should I suspect first?
pool.p11: The uplink keeps flapping up and down — is it okay to just leave it?
pool.p12: I suspect a loop between switches — how do I isolate it?
pool.p13: I changed a VLAN and now clients can't reach anything — where do I check?
pool.p14: It says a switch's config is out of sync with what Central expects — what does that actually mean?
pool.p15: What goes wrong if I don't enable Protected Management Frames (PMF)?
pool.p16: I can't decide between MPSK and PSK — is there a rule of thumb?
pool.p17: I want to audit our SSIDs — what should I check?
pool.p18: What should drive the cipher suite choice?
pool.p19: What's the actual difference between WIDS/WIPS Detection and Protection?
pool.p20: A site's health score suddenly dropped — where do I start looking?
pool.p21: The counts don't match between Central's summary and the alert list — is that a bug?
pool.p22: Several devices seem to have gone down at once — where do I even begin?
pool.p23: The same alert keeps firing — how do I tell if it's a false positive?
pool.p24: Someone says airtime utilization is high and things feel slow — what should I check?
pool.p25: The WAN link seems to flap occasionally — is it fine to just watch it?
pool.p26: An AP keeps rebooting on its own — what should I check first?

quiz.title: Quiz
quiz.empty: Hit 'Give me a question' and I'll build one from a real case of ours.
quiz.placeholder: Write whatever comes to mind. It doesn't have to be tidy.

evidence.title: What this came from ({n})
evidence.locked: There are {n} records behind this. You'll be able to open them once we've checked the answer.
evidence.citedTitle: Coach actually leaned on this one for this reply

weakness.title: Where you've been getting stuck
weakness.rule: Only topics you've hit {n}+ times count as a weak spot
weakness.empty: Nothing recorded yet. Try talking something through, or take a quiz.
weakness.watchingNote: Still watching (not enough attempts to call it a weak spot)
weakness.effect: On your weak topics I start hints one step further in, and get to the answer sooner.

error.emptyPool: Couldn't find anything to ask about. Approve some knowledge entries, or run a few investigations.
error.noActiveQuiz: No question in progress. Hit 'Give me a question' again.
error.materialGone: The record behind this question is gone. Let's move to the next one.
error.sessionNotFound: That record could not be found.

live.badgeTitle: This reply is grounded in facts retrieved from Central / Mist just now (tools called: {tools})
live.on: When our own records are thin, I go and ask Central / Mist for the current state
live.off: Live check is off right now (answers come from past records only)
